answer: Paragraph 14 places “upon SFC’s request” with demonstration; confirmation is not expressly request-conditioned. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity. Demonstration expressly carries the standard “to the SFC’s satisfaction”. Footnote 5 adds minimum content for confirmation and demonstration: compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and assurance, with a high level of confidence, against smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws. Its omission of the request condition leaves competing readings. Reading C harmonises the provisions by applying the footnote’s minimum content to standing confirmation and request-triggered demonstration; reading B treats the footnote as requiring standing demonstration too. Reading A preserves the main-text trigger while leaving the footnote’s attachment unresolved. Without a request, A and C do not trigger demonstration, whereas B does; confirmation and applicable underlying requirements remain. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on the relevant SFC request. None of these applicability conclusions establishes fulfillment.

claims.inference: Textual attachment: the intervening request phrase modifies demonstration. The satisfaction phrase directly follows demonstration; extending it independently to confirmation requires interpretation.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the Product Provider, product, activity and assessment interval.
Any applicable authorisation conditions, amendments or additional SFC requirements.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 distinguishes unconditionally worded confirmation from request-triggered demonstration of the same three subjects, with demonstration to the SFC’s satisfaction.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

claims.inference: The footnote expressly addresses both verbs and specifies minimum content. Grammatically, “with a high level of confidence” most directly qualifies the smart-contract assurance; it does not supply a numerical threshold or expressly replace SFC satisfaction.
missing_premises: An authoritative resolution of how the footnote’s unqualified demonstration language interacts with the main-text request condition.
The applicable evidential meaning of high confidence and SFC satisfaction.
claims.proposition: Footnote 5 expands the stated content to at least compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.
claims.status: Express minimum content; trigger and standard attachment partly interpretive

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

claims.inference: Assuming positively established absence of a relevant request, demonstration is untriggered under A and C but remains standing under B. Absence of a request does not remove confirmation or the separately stated underlying requirements. Missing request evidence alone does not establish that no request exists.
missing_premises: Actual request history, including the scope and timing of any request.
Selection and justification of the governing reading.
Evidence that confirmation and the underlying requirements have actually been fulfilled.
claims.proposition: No request has different consequences under the rival demonstration readings and does not establish compliance.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction
Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

claims.inference: Paragraph 15 specifies obtaining external audit or verification, rather than simply confirming or demonstrating. The relevant request must cover that activity; a paragraph 14 request does not automatically establish this trigger, although one request could expressly cover both.
missing_premises: An applicable request for third-party audit or verification.
The request’s scope and evidence of the audit or verification obtained.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 15 expressly conditions obtaining third-party audit or verification of the same three subjects on SFC request.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.

claims.inference: The requested object is a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. This is distinct from paragraph 14 demonstration and paragraph 15 technical or operational audit or verification; the sentence does not itself define satisfactory opinion content.
missing_premises: An applicable request for a legal opinion supporting the identified application.
The applicable satisfaction standard and evidence that the opinion meets it.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 16 expressly conditions obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application on SFC request.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: confirmation stands without a request; demonstration of the paragraph 14 subjects is request-triggered and to SFC satisfaction. Footnote 5’s precise effect on content and standards remains unresolved.

B — Standing-footnote reading: the unqualified words “confirm and demonstrate” support standing demonstration of the footnote’s minimum content, even without a request. This encounters the express main-text request condition and needs a justification for that interaction.

C — Harmonised reading: footnote 5 supplies minimum content for both confirmation and demonstration, while paragraph 14 supplies the request trigger and SFC-satisfaction standard for demonstration. This gives effect to both texts but remains an interpretive judgment.
unresolved: The retained text does not conclusively settle the conflict between the main-text request condition and the footnote’s unqualified demonstration wording.
Confirmation’s timing, form and evidential requirements are not specified here; standing does not necessarily mean continuous submission.
The exact reach of the high-confidence qualification and its practical relationship to SFC satisfaction require an applicable standard.
Entity roles, temporal applicability, request facts and actual performance evidence are absent. Applicability cannot establish fulfillment.
Reported parsing, graph acceptance and serialization results cannot resolve legal interpretation or certify legal correctness.
